slot.brief: At hard difficulty: ask about zwitterion behaviour and pH-dependent charge of amino acids with acidic/basic side chains, or which amino acid lacks a chiral centre.

stem: At pH well below all ionisation $pK_\mathrm{a}$ values and well above them, respectively, what are the net charges of aspartic acid and lysine? Give each pair in low-to-high pH order.

verdicts.working: At low pH, Asp has two neutral COOH groups and one NH₃⁺ (+1); at high pH, it has two COO⁻ groups (−2). Lys has two NH₃⁺ groups (+2) at low pH and one COO⁻ (−1) at high pH.

working:
Aspartic acid: low pH, $\text{NH}_3^+$ and two $\text{COOH}$ groups give $+1$; high pH, two $\text{COO}^-$ groups give $-2$.\nLysine: low pH, two $\text{NH}_3^+$ groups give $+2$; high pH, one $\text{COO}^-$ gives $-1$.

Independent check: At low pH, Asp has two neutral COOH groups and one NH₃⁺ (+1); at high pH, it has two COO⁻ groups (−2). Lys has two NH₃⁺ groups (+2) at low pH and one COO⁻ (−1) at high pH.
solution:
At low pH, carboxyl groups are neutral ($\mathrm{COOH}$) and amino groups are protonated ($\mathrm{NH_3^+}$); at high pH, carboxyl groups are $\mathrm{COO^-}$ and amino groups are neutral.
$$\text{Aspartic acid: }(+1,-2),\qquad \text{Lysine: }(+2,-1)$$
